Order 
1. Petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323 and 506 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. The case of the prosecution is that the petitioners herein subjected the de-facto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically.
3. Respondent no.2 is present before this Court and represented by her learned counsel.

4. The petitioners have annexed a copy of the memorandum of settlement dated 19.07.2023 under Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005.
A perusal of the memorandum of settlement indicated that the defacto complainant had filed a suit in O.S.No.22/2023 for dissolving her marriage with accused no.1.
The matter was referred to the Mediation Centre to NC: 2023:KHC:41017 explore the possibility of settlement between the parties.

Before the Mediation Centre, the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and in terms of the settlement, their marriage has been dissolved mutually, and accused no.1 has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lakhs only) to the de-facto complainant towards permanent alimony out of which Rs.2,50,000/- is already paid and the balance amount of Rs.2,50,000/- will be paid as per the terms of the settlement.

5. Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against them will be an abuse of the process of law.
Accordingly, the criminal petition is allowed.
The impugned proceedings in CC No.54613/2020 on the file of 29th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayo Hall at Bengaluru stands quashed.
